final:
STATUS: fail
SUMMARY: One reproduced blocking failure: the hours table overflows at 360px as soon as a cell holds realistic longer text, because `.hours-table td` is `white-space: nowrap`. Shipped content passes every other check I ran (contrast, overflow, keyboard, URL state, date sweep, form edge cases). Test coverage has gaps, and the test runner's chronology check can't detect a missing sort.
FILES TOUCHED: none in the repo (`git status` still shows the same 13 entries). Probes are in /tmp/claude-0/-tmp-ff-eval-mv-e9x3f-workspace/c64675ad-fb1b-4e3e-befa-7d8c152cb78c/scratchpad/probe and a mutated copy in .../scratchpad/mut.
FINDINGS:
- [blocking] Hours table overflows at 360px with realistic hours text. Setting the Sunday cell to "Closed for stocktake the first Sunday of each month" gives `documentElement.scrollWidth` 483 at 360px. "Late opening Thursdays until 20:00" gives a table 6px wider than its container. Cause: `.hours-table td { white-space: nowrap }`. Shipped content passes (360 scrollWidth 360). This is the hostile "fixed-width table (hours)" input, so I rate it blocking.
- [minor] `#form-status` is an empty, always-visible bar before any submit (24px tall, tinted background, 4px dark left border).
- [minor] JS off: no books, no genre filter, no result count, no events, no home picks, and the books page gives no explanation. The contact form, with JS off, submits as a GET to `visit.html?name=&email=&message=` with no feedback.
- [minor] At 23:59 local on 21 Nov (America/Los_Angeles), the 19:00 event is still listed as upcoming. The date-only comparison is day-granular.
- [minor] Test gaps: `events-are-chronological` still passes with the sort removed, because the shipped data is already sorted. `books-empty-state` only checks hidden text. No test covers body-text contrast, 320px, or reduced motion (the media block is a no-op; there are no transitions).
- [minor] Radio arrow keys push a history entry per step. Two ArrowDowns then Back lands on the intermediate genre.
- [minor] A 5000-character mailto body is about 8.3k characters, so mail clients may truncate it silently. Not reproduced in a real mail client.
- [minor] Escape always moves focus to the Menu button, even when focus has already left the open menu. Read from code, not reproduced.
CHECKS:
- Computed-colour audit, every text node, all four pages at 360 (menu open) and 1280, plus input borders → min text 7.15:1, no failures (pass).
- scrollWidth at 320 and 360, closed and open menu, all pages → equals viewport (pass).
- 300-char unbroken token into every text element at 360 → only hours `td` cells widen the page (fail, see above).
- Keyboard-only menu at 320: Enter opens, Tab reaches links, Escape closes and returns focus to toggle (pass).
- Radio arrows update URL and count; Back restores previous genre (pass).
- Property test: 1410 `?genre=` values (fixed hostile set + seeded random, via popstate) and 300 real radio clicks; checks count, card count, checked radio, URL, no injected nodes, no dialogs → 0 failures (pass).
- Events/home sweep: 3 zones × 151 days × 2 times, lists equal events dated today or later → 0 mismatches (pass).
- Mutation: UTC-parsed date filter → `events-include-event-on-local-midnight` fails (pass, test has power).
- Mutation: drop `aria-describedby` → `form-empty-submit` fails (pass).
- Mutation: drop event sort → chronological test passes (weak test, see above).
- Form edges: whitespace-only name/message rejected; "a b@c.com" and "x" rejected; trailing-space email accepted; `&` and `#` in subject encoded; double submit keeps demo wording (pass).
- Lorem/external URL grep across HTML/CSS/JS → none (pass). External-request test in runner passes (pass, per orchestrator).
- Triggered checks: Focus/keyboard (menu, Escape, radio) ran as above (pass). Invariants (property test) ran as above (pass). Money: n/a, prices are static and formatted with fixed two decimals. Command output: n/a, no CLI.
- Project checklist: keyboard and focus (pass), 360px (fail, hours table), form labels and errors (pass), URL state (pass), no external requests (pass), real content (pass), decorative elements (status bar only).
OPEN QUESTIONS: (1) Is the hours-table overflow blocking, given that shipped content passes and the hostile input is a content edit rather than user input? I rated it blocking because the criteria name it explicitly. (2) Is JS-off degradation in scope? The criteria don't mention it.
